sources.title: Plan migration from Azure Communication Services
Set up inbound calling for the voice channel
Transfer calls and consult with users
Configure call recording, transcription, and real-time translation
Manage overflow of work items in queues
Configure conversation orchestration in Dynamics 365 Contact Center
Set up outbound calling in the voice channel
Disconnect from Azure Communication Services resources
Integrate a non-Microsoft IVR system with voice channel
Configure customer-first direct callback in Dynamics 365 Contact Center
Dial modes for proactive engagement in Dynamics 365 Contact Center
Use APIs to pause, resume transcription and recording
Deployment approaches for voice channel in Dynamics 365 Contact Center
Use overflow actions to protect customer experience for direct inward calls
Consult, transfer securely for PSTN numbers, and IVR

questions.prompt:
Sallow Bay Assurance embeds calling in a non-Microsoft CRM. Its developers control call capture through the voice module of the Dynamics 365 Contact Center CCaaS SDK.

On claims calls, the CRM must start the audio recording and the transcript together, using as few voice module method calls as possible.

You need to start capture on claims calls.

Which call or calls should the CRM make?

options.text: startRecording only
startTranscription only
startRecording, and then startTranscription
startRecording, and then startTranscription after onRecordingOperationCompleted fires

questions.explanation: The voice module doesn't split the two evenly. startRecording initiates voice call recording with automatic transcription, so one method call covers both. startTranscription begins transcription without full recording, so it can't supply the audio. Adding startTranscription, with or without waiting for a callback, only adds method calls, which the requirement rules out.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. startRecording initiates voice call recording with automatic transcription, so one method call covers both.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. startTranscription begins transcription without full recording, so the audio would be missing.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. startRecording already includes automatic transcription, so the extra startTranscription call breaks the requirement for as few method calls as possible.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. startRecording already includes automatic transcription, so the callback and the startTranscription call are extra method calls, which the requirement rules out.

questions.prompt:
Tolbury Water has a voice proactive engagement that uses the CCaaS API intake method. Its consent, opt-out and quiet hours processes are in place.

Three new integrations will create deliveries, and none of them may use a first-generation API.

You need to choose the API for each integration.

Which API should each integration call?

rows.label: The billing system sends one request per household, with up to four account holders to dial as a linked chain
A nightly job sends about 12,000 unrelated customers in a single request
A Power Automate flow passes one customer as flat fields, without nested JSON

questions.answer: Household chain: CCaaS_CreateProactiveDelivery. Nightly job: CCaaS_CreateProactiveBulkDelivery. Power Automate flow: CCaaS_CreateSimpleProactiveDelivery.
questions.explanation: Microsoft separates these APIs by the shape of the request. CCaaS_CreateProactiveDelivery is the most versatile and supports account calling, with one to five contacts in a voice request. CCaaS_CreateProactiveBulkDelivery takes approximately 15,000 records in one request, but it does not support account calling, so it suits unrelated customers. CCaaS_CreateSimpleProactiveDelivery handles a single recipient with flattened attributes and is best suited to surfaces like Power Automate. CCaaS_CreateProactiveVoiceDelivery is the first-generation voice API, which the stem excludes.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for the household chain. This API supports account calling, and a voice request can carry one to five contacts. That limit rules it out for the nightly job.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for the nightly job. It sends approximately 15,000 records in a single request. It does not support account calling, so it fails for the household chain.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for the Power Automate flow. It provides flattened attributes for a single recipient and does not require complex JSON nesting. The single recipient rules it out for the other two integrations.
optionExplanations.d: Fails on every row. This is the first-generation voice API, which the stem excludes. Microsoft advises migrating from it to CCaaS_CreateProactiveDelivery for the latest features.

questions.prompt:
Greyfriars Energy uses Teams Phone extensibility numbers. It runs proactive voice engagements for service outreach only, with none for marketing or sales, and its legal team has cleared each program under the applicable telecommunications rules. About 40 representatives are normally available, and a Copilot Studio agent is on the outbound workstream.

Three outreach programs are planned.

You need to choose the dial mode for each program.

Which dial mode should you use for each program?

rows.label: Planned outage notices: hundreds of calls run at once, and the AI agent finishes nearly every call without a representative
Hardship plan follow-ups: a representative reads the account and starts each call when ready, because a personal conversation matters more than representative use
Meter access rescheduling: every customer talks to a representative, and calls start ahead of representatives becoming free to keep them fully used

questions.answer: Planned outage notices: Copilot. Hardship plan follow-ups: Preview. Meter access rescheduling: Predictive.
questions.explanation: Each mode balances AI involvement, representative use and customer experience differently. Copilot suits announcements and notifications that an IVR agent can handle, and many calls can run at once. Preview notifies a representative first and allows time to review details, so it puts customer experience ahead of representative use. Predictive starts calls before representatives are free, based on when they are forecast to be free. Progressive works from the representatives who are available now, so it does not run ahead of them, and it brings a representative onto the call, so it does not suit notices the AI agent finishes alone.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for outage notices. Copilot mode is for announcements and notifications that an IVR agent can handle, and a large number of calls can run at once. The agent escalates to a representative only if necessary.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for hardship follow-ups. The representative is notified first and gets time to review the details. On Teams Phone extensibility numbers, the call can wait until the representative starts it.
optionExplanations.c: Fails on every program. It works from the representatives who are available now, so it does not start calls on a forecast of when they will be free. Both of its engagement types bring a representative onto the call, and neither gives the representative time to review before dialing.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for rescheduling. Predictive initiates calls before representatives are available, based on when they are forecast to be free. It needs at least 10 available representatives, and Greyfriars normally has about 40.

questions.prompt:
Hartwell Pharmacy wants recording and transcription to differ by type of call. Its main line is connected to a voice workstream. Each pharmacist has a personal number with an inbound profile. The shared Refills number has an outbound profile.

You need to identify where to change the transcription and recording setting for each type of call.

Where should you change the setting for each type of call?

tokens.text: The Behaviors tab of the voice workstream
The inbound profile for that number
The outbound profile for that number

rows.label: Customers phone the main line and are routed through queues
Customers phone a pharmacist's personal number directly
Pharmacists call customers from the shared Refills number
Pharmacists call customers from their personal numbers

questions.answer: Main line: the Behaviors tab of the voice workstream. Direct calls to a personal number: the inbound profile for that number. Calls from the Refills number: the outbound profile for that number. Calls from personal numbers: the default scoped outbound profile.
questions.explanation: The setting lives with whatever defines the call path. A queue-routed line takes its capture settings from the voice workstream. Direct inward dialing and outbound calling from a shared number are defined by profiles, and each profile type has its own transcription and recording setting. Personal numbers are the trap: they can have an inbound profile for calls in, but an outbound profile can only list numbers that are not used as personal numbers, and Microsoft says personal number calls always apply the default scoped outbound profile.

optionExplanations.a: Correct for the main line. The Transcription and recording section is on the Behaviors tab of the voice settings for the workstream.
optionExplanations.b: Correct for direct calls. Each inbound profile has a Transcription and recording setting under Inbound behaviors.
optionExplanations.c: Correct for the Refills number. The outbound profile holds Transcription and recording under Outbound behaviors. It fails for personal numbers, because the outbound profile number list excludes numbers used as personal numbers.
optionExplanations.d: Correct for calls placed from personal numbers. Microsoft says personal number calls always apply the default scoped outbound profile, and outbound profiles hold Transcription and recording under Outbound behaviors.
optionExplanations.e: Fails on every row. That page covers the call quality survey, automatic un-hold, DTMF broadcast and external contact overrides. It does not hold the general capture choice for a call path.

questions.prompt:
Millbrook Home Services runs its voice channel on Teams Phone numbers. Its Boiler Repairs voice queue has no overflow actions yet. During winter peaks, callers should be able to leave the queue. The system should then call them first and connect a representative only after a Copilot Studio agent verifies them.

The Microsoft Copilot Studio agent is provisioned in the environment, the verification agent is built, and numbers with outbound calling are configured. Management accepts that customer-first direct callback cannot be turned off after it is enabled.

You need to enable customer-first direct callback and apply it to the Boiler Repairs queue.

Which three actions should you perform, and in what order?

tokens.text: On the Boiler Repairs queue, select Direct callback as an overflow action, and then select the callback profile.
Edit the provisioned Callback Agent in Copilot Studio so that it runs the customer verification.
On the Callback management page, enable Copilot AI agent for callback management, and wait for Callback Agent to provision.
On the workstream's fallback queue, select Direct callback as the overflow action.
Turn on the Customer-first direct callback toggle, and then create and save the first callback profile.

questions.answer: 1. Enable Copilot AI agent for callback management and wait for Callback Agent to provision. 2. Turn on the Customer-first direct callback toggle, and then create and save the first callback profile. 3. Select Direct callback as an overflow action on the Boiler Repairs queue, and then select the callback profile.
questions.explanation: Each step needs the one before it. The toggle is selected after Callback Agent finishes provisioning. Customer-first direct callback is enabled only when the first callback profile is saved, and saving it is what makes the profile available for queue configuration. A queue can then point its Direct callback overflow action at that profile. Millbrook has no overflow action on the queue yet, so the first profile is not applied to it automatically. The verification agent is selected inside the callback profile, so Callback Agent is left alone.

optionExplanations.a: Third step. The queue selects a callback profile, so a saved profile must already exist.
optionExplanations.b: Not a step. Microsoft warns against editing or deleting the AI agent configured for taking the alternative number, because changes might stop callback working as expected. Your own agent is selected in the callback profile instead.
optionExplanations.c: First step. The Customer-first direct callback toggle is selected after provisioning completes.
optionExplanations.d: Not a step. The system ignores the overflow settings of a fallback queue, and the requirement concerns the Boiler Repairs queue.
optionExplanations.e: Second step. The feature cannot be enabled until at least one callback profile exists, and saving the first profile makes it available for queue configuration.

questions.prompt:
Ferncliff Bank is moving its voice service to Teams Phone extensibility in phases. Retail Banking still uses Azure Communication Services Direct Routing numbers. Card Services already uses Teams Phone extensibility with Teams Direct Routing numbers.

The bank has three new requirements for this phase.

You need to choose the numbers that support each requirement.

Which numbers should you use for each requirement?

rows.label: A preview engagement in which each call starts after a countdown that begins when a representative accepts

options.text: Azure Communication Services numbers
Teams Phone extensibility numbers
Either platform's numbers

rows.label: The callback number for customers who phoned Retail Banking and chose customer-first direct callback

options.text: Azure Communication Services numbers
Teams Phone extensibility numbers
Either platform's numbers

rows.label: A new outbound workstream that dials from Operator Connect numbers

options.text: Azure Communication Services numbers
Teams Phone extensibility numbers
Either platform's numbers

questions.answer: Preview countdown: Teams Phone extensibility numbers. Callback for Retail Banking callers: Azure Communication Services numbers. Outbound workstream with Operator Connect numbers: Teams Phone extensibility numbers.
questions.explanation: During a phased migration, the two platforms are not interchangeable. The preview timer and delayed start are available on Teams Phone Extensibility only, and on Azure Communication Services a preview call starts as soon as the representative accepts. A callback must use the same phone platform as the inbound call, because a callback from a Teams number to a customer who called an Azure Communication Services number is never initiated and the request closes. An outbound workstream on Azure Communication Services supports Direct Routing numbers only, while Teams Phone also supports Direct Offer and Operator Connect numbers.

optionExplanations.r1a: Fails. On Azure Communication Services, preview calls start automatically after the representative accepts the invite, so there is no countdown.
optionExplanations.r1b: Correct. The timer and delayed start for preview calls are available on Teams Phone Extensibility only.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. The countdown depends on the platform, and only Teams Phone Extensibility numbers offer it.
optionExplanations.r2a: Correct. These customers phoned an Azure Communication Services number, and inbound calls and outbound callbacks must use the same phone platform.
optionExplanations.r2b: Fails. If a customer calls an Azure Communication Services number and the callback uses a Teams number, the system does not initiate the callback and closes the request.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. Mixing platforms stops the callback, so the choice is not free.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. For outbound workstreams, Azure Communication Services supports Direct Routing numbers only.
optionExplanations.r3b: Correct. Teams Phone supports Direct Routing, Direct Offer and Operator Connect numbers on an outbound workstream.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. Operator Connect numbers are supported on Teams Phone only.

questions.prompt:
Ravenscar Health Plans records and transcribes voice calls automatically. Its Member Services workstream has External phone numbers selected for Consult and Transfer, and Use bridged transfers is on. The External Contact Settings section on the Voice call experiences page, which Microsoft documents as a production-ready preview, is available.

Ravenscar is adding its Clinical Review and Identity Check numbers as external contacts.

You need to choose the Hold configuration for each situation.

What should you choose for each situation?

rows.label: Consult with Clinical Review: representatives discuss a claim with a nurse, the member must not hear it, and no representative may lift the hold

options.text: Customer on hold
Agent on hold
Follow workstream settings
No Hold setting applies

rows.label: Consult with Identity Check: the member answers security questions on the line, and representatives must not hear the answers

options.text: Customer on hold
Agent on hold
Follow workstream settings
No Hold setting applies

rows.label: Bridged transfer to Identity Check

options.text: Customer on hold
Agent on hold
Follow workstream settings
No Hold setting applies

questions.answer: Consult with Clinical Review: Customer on hold. Consult with Identity Check: Agent on hold. Bridged transfer to Identity Check: no Hold setting applies.
questions.explanation: The Hold option decides who is kept out of the secure conversation, and it applies to consult only. Customer on hold keeps the member out while representatives talk to the contact, and a representative cannot remove that hold. Agent on hold does the reverse: every representative on the call is held while the member interacts with the contact. Follow workstream settings adds no such lock. A bridged transfer has its own Transcription and recording choice but no Hold choice.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. The customer is placed on hold automatically during the secure consult, and the representative cannot remove the hold.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. This holds the representatives and leaves the member with the contact, which is the opposite of what the row needs.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. It inherits the workstream configuration, and in an ordinary consult the primary representative removes the customer from hold manually, so the hold could be lifted.
optionExplanations.r1d: Fails. This is a consult, and Hold applies to consult, so without a locked setting a representative could lift the hold.
optionExplanations.r2a: Fails. This holds the member, who has to answer the questions on the line.
optionExplanations.r2b: Correct. Representatives are placed on hold during the secure consult, so the member can interact with the contact privately, and they cannot modify the hold.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. It inherits the workstream configuration, and an ordinary consult puts the customer on hold, not the representatives.
optionExplanations.r2d: Fails. This is a consult, and Hold applies to consult, so without Agent on hold the representatives aren't held.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. Hold is not a bridged transfer setting.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. Hold is not a bridged transfer setting, and the representative leaves the call in a bridged transfer.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. Hold is not a bridged transfer setting, so there is nothing to inherit here.
optionExplanations.r3d: Correct. The Hold setting applies to consult only. Bridged transfer offers the Transcription and recording choice.

questions.prompt:
Brightmoor Holidays plans staffing for three voice queues with one short-term forecast scenario. The Workforce Management for Customer Service package is installed. Each queue has a Historical End Date of January 31. The scenario has a Forecast Start Date of February 7 and a duration of 30 days.

The available history for each queue is listed in calendar days.

You need to predict how forecasting treats each queue.

What is the result for each queue?

rows.label: Bookings: 40 days of history

options.text: Forecast generated normally
Forecast generated with reduced confidence
Queue skipped with no forecast

rows.label: Refunds: 33 days of history

options.text: Forecast generated normally
Forecast generated with reduced confidence
Queue skipped with no forecast

rows.label: Group Travel: 28 days of history

options.text: Forecast generated normally
Forecast generated with reduced confidence
Queue skipped with no forecast

questions.answer: Bookings: forecast generated normally. Refunds: forecast generated with reduced confidence. Group Travel: queue skipped with no forecast.
questions.explanation: The days between the Historical End Date and the Forecast Start Date are the gap, here February 1 through February 6, or six days. Forecasting has to predict those hidden days too, so a short-term scenario needs the gap plus the duration, which is 36 days. Bookings meets that. Refunds falls short, so the grace rules decide: the gap is within half the duration, 15 days, and 33 days meets the 30-day baseline, so it gets a forecast with reduced confidence and the Insufficient Historical Data flag. Group Travel is below the baseline, so it is skipped even though the gap is within the grace period.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. 40 days meets the gap-adjusted requirement of 36 days, so the grace rules are not needed.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. Reduced confidence applies only when history falls short of the gap-adjusted requirement.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. A queue is skipped only when history falls short and a grace condition is not met.
optionExplanations.r2a: Fails. 33 days meets the 30-day baseline but not the 36 days required once the gap is counted.
optionExplanations.r2b: Correct. History is short of 36 days, the six-day gap is within the 15-day grace period, and 33 days meets the 30-day baseline.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. Both grace conditions are met, so the forecast is still generated.
optionExplanations.r3a: Fails. 28 days is below both the 36-day requirement and the 30-day baseline.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. Reduced confidence needs history that meets the baseline, and 28 days is below 30.
optionExplanations.r3c: Correct. History is below the 30-day baseline, so one grace condition fails and forecasting skips the queue.

questions.prompt:
Pennine Broadband creates voice deliveries with CCaaS_CreateProactiveDelivery and stores the DeliveryId and DeliveryTaskId from each response. One engagement serves customers across the country, with reattempts and contact chaining.

Three situations arise after a network fault.

You need to stop the right calls in each situation and leave all other calls in place.

What should you use for each situation?

rows.label: A household reports that its fault is fixed, so nobody in that contact chain should get any further attempt

options.text: CCaaS_CancelDeliveryTask with the DeliveryTaskId
CCaaS_CreateOperation with Cancel and the DeliveryId
A cancellation policy filtered by postal code

rows.label: The first dial in a new request went in by mistake, and only that dial should be canceled

options.text: CCaaS_CancelDeliveryTask with the DeliveryTaskId
CCaaS_CreateOperation with Cancel and the DeliveryId
A cancellation policy filtered by postal code

rows.label: A flood hits one state, so queued calls there must stop and no new calls may start there until Friday

options.text: A cancellation policy filtered by state, with an Execute policy until date
CCaaS_CreateOperation with Suspend and the engagement configuration ID
CCaaS_CancelDeliveryTask with each DeliveryTaskId in that state

questions.answer: Household chain: CCaaS_CancelDeliveryTask with the DeliveryTaskId. One mistaken dial: CCaaS_CreateOperation with Cancel and the DeliveryId. Flood in one state: a cancellation policy filtered by state, with an Execute policy until date.
questions.explanation: The three tools differ by scope. DeliveryTaskId identifies the task that manages the contact chain and all reattempts, so CCaaS_CancelDeliveryTask stops every pending and future attempt for that contact or account. DeliveryId identifies the first individual dial, so CCaaS_CreateOperation with Cancel stops that delivery. A cancellation policy works on criteria instead of IDs: it cancels queued calls that match, and with Execute policy until it also keeps matching contacts from being processed for new calls during that period.

optionExplanations.r1a: Correct. This cancels all pending and future delivery attempts for a contact or account, so no further attempts are made.
optionExplanations.r1b: Fails. The DeliveryId identifies one dial, so canceling it does not cover the whole chain and its reattempts.
optionExplanations.r1c: Fails. A postal code matches neighboring customers too, and the other calls must stay in place.
optionExplanations.r2a: Fails. This cancels every pending and future attempt in the chain, not only one dial.
optionExplanations.r2b: Correct. The DeliveryId identifies the first individual dial, and the Cancel operation cancels that delivery.
optionExplanations.r2c: Fails. A policy works on matching criteria and would catch other customers. It cannot target one dial.
optionExplanations.r3a: Correct. A cancellation policy can filter by state, and Execute policy until keeps matching contacts from being processed for new calls during that period.
optionExplanations.r3b: Fails. Suspend is requested for the engagement, which serves the whole country, so it would stop calls that must continue.
optionExplanations.r3c: Fails. Each call cancels an existing task, so nothing stops new calls from starting in that state until Friday.

questions.prompt:
Stanmore Couriers runs its voice channel on Teams Phone extensibility, with Teams Direct Routing through its own SBC. It plans a representative-led predictive engagement to reschedule missed deliveries. Use bridged transfers is selected on every voice workstream, and the legal team has cleared the outreach.

You need to confirm that the SBC can handle the call-transfer flows that this dial mode relies on.

Which three capabilities should you confirm? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: It accepts INVITE messages with Require: replaces and Replaces headers under RFC 3891.
It handles P-Asserted-Identity with Privacy ID under RFC 3325.
It trusts every supported root CA for Teams SIP interface certificates.
It turns a REFER-TO: sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com request into an INVITE back to the hub.
It trusts only the root CA that issued the current Teams SIP interface certificate.

questions.answer: RFC 3891 Replaces support, RFC 3325 handling of P-Asserted-Identity with Privacy ID, and every supported root CA for Teams SIP interface certificates in the trust store.
questions.explanation: Representative-led progressive and predictive modes depend on mid-call transfer flows, so Microsoft lists SBC requirements for direct routing. The SBC must support RFC 3891 Replaces headers, including INVITE messages with Require: replaces. It must support RFC 3325 handling for P-Asserted-Identity with Privacy ID. Its trust store must include all supported root CAs, because Teams SIP interface certificates can chain to any one of them. The REFER-TO conversion belongs to a different case: external transfers when Use bridged transfers is not selected.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. Microsoft calls this capability essential for the mid-call transfer flows used in progressive and predictive dial modes.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. RFC 3325 handling for P-Asserted-Identity with Privacy ID is on the list for these dial modes.
optionExplanations.c: Correct. Teams SIP interface certificates can chain to any supported root CA, so the trust store must include them all.
optionExplanations.d: Fails here. This configuration applies to Direct Routing customers when Use bridged transfers is not selected, and Stanmore has it selected on every workstream.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Certificates can chain to any of the supported roots, so trusting one root could break the connection when a certificate chains to another.

questions.prompt:
Cloudberry Mobile turned on the Customer service representative call quality survey on the Voice call experiences page and set how often it appears. Representatives have answered it for a month. Analysts now want to review the answers, but no responses can be found.

You need to make sure that future survey responses are kept for analysis.

Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: In Azure Monitor, enable the Call Survey Logs diagnostic setting, and send the logs to a Log Analytics workspace.
In Azure Monitor, enable the Call Survey Logs diagnostic setting, and send the logs to an Azure storage account.
In Azure Monitor, enable the Call Summary logs diagnostic setting, and send the logs to a Log Analytics workspace.
On the Voice call experiences page, turn on Set survey duration, and specify a longer duration for the survey.
On the voice workstream, turn on the Post-call survey toggle, and complete the post-call survey setup steps.

questions.answer: Enable the Call Survey Logs diagnostic setting in Azure Monitor, and send the logs to either a Log Analytics workspace or an Azure storage account.
questions.explanation: Turning on the survey only collects the answers. Unless the Call Survey Logs diagnostic setting sends them to a Log Analytics workspace, Event Hubs or an Azure storage account, they are not stored and can be lost. Either listed destination keeps future responses, and earlier responses cannot be recovered this way because data is not stored retroactively. The other settings look related, but they cover other logs, how long the survey is shown, or the customer survey.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. A Log Analytics workspace is a supported destination for the survey data, and it can be queried for analysis.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. An Azure storage account is a supported destination for the survey data, and it also keeps the responses.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. The right destination does not help with the wrong log. Survey data needs the Call Survey category, not Call Summary.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Set survey duration controls how long the survey appears for the representative. It does not store responses.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. The post-call survey is for customers. It does not store the representative call quality survey.

questions.prompt:
Saltash Ferries is giving up two Azure Communication Services numbers. The Bookings number is connected to a voice workstream, and it is also the number on an outbound profile. The Harbour Desk number is assigned to a representative as a personal number. Saltash will keep its other numbers on the same resource.

You need to prepare both numbers so that they can be released.

Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.

options.text: Remove the Bookings number from the voice workstream.
Remove the Bookings number from the outbound profile.
Disable the Harbour Desk number.
Clear Make calls from the Bookings number calling plan.
Disconnect the Azure Communication Services resource.

questions.answer: Remove the Bookings number from the voice workstream and from the outbound profile, and disable the Harbour Desk number.
questions.explanation: Releasing a number deletes it from Dynamics 365, so Microsoft requires the number to be free of its uses first. Remove it from any associated workstreams or outbound profiles. If it is assigned as a personal number, disable it and then try releasing it again. Calling plan features cannot be removed once granted. Disconnecting the resource is a much larger action, because all phone numbers associated with that resource are released.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. A number must be removed from any associated workstreams before it is released.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. A number must also be removed from any associated outbound profiles.
optionExplanations.c: Correct. A number assigned as a personal number must be disabled before it can be released.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Features cannot be removed once granted to a phone number, and the plan is not a release requirement.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. Disconnecting a resource also releases all phone numbers associated with it, and Saltash is keeping its other numbers.

questions.prompt:
Hollins Department Stores moved its voice service to Dynamics 365 Contact Center last month, so Dynamics 365 holds very little workload history. Its retired workforce management application exported two intraday CSV files that match Microsoft's templates. One holds 18 months of voice volume and handle time. The other holds that application's forecast of volume and handle time for the next six weeks. The Workforce Management package is installed, and you have the WFM Administrator role.

You need a short-term capacity plan whose demand comes from the retired application's data.

Which two approaches should you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.text: Upload the history as External historical data for forecast scenario, create a short-term External forecast scenario with Auto refresh turned off, and select that scenario in the capacity plan after its first forecast run.
Upload the forecast as External forecast data for capacity planning, create the short-term capacity plan with the external file source, and select the file in External forecast file.
Upload the forecast as Capacity plan parameter override, create the capacity plan from a forecast scenario with the Internal data source, and select the file in Capacity plan parameter override.

Upload the history as External historical data for forecast scenario, create a short-term External forecast scenario with Auto refresh turned on, and select that scenario in the capacity plan after its first forecast run.
Create a short-term forecast scenario with the Internal data source and a Historical data start date 18 months back, and select that scenario in the capacity plan after its first forecast run.

questions.answer: Either upload the history as External historical data for forecast scenario and base the capacity plan on an External forecast scenario, or upload the forecast as External forecast data for capacity planning and select it as the plan's external forecast file.
questions.explanation: The file type decides which capability consumes the data. External historical data trains a Dynamics 365 forecast scenario, which a capacity plan can use once it has completed a forecast run. External forecast data skips forecast generation and feeds the capacity plan directly. A parameter override only changes service assumptions and handle time, so it cannot supply volume. An External scenario can't use Auto refresh, so it isn't refreshed on a schedule.

optionExplanations.a: Correct. This is the route for history kept outside Dynamics 365. The forecast scenario trains on the file, and a capacity plan can use the scenario after it has completed a forecast run. Auto refresh isn't available with an external data source, so it stays off.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. This is the route when a forecast already exists in another system. It skips forecast generation and uses the file as the demand input.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. An override file carries service assumptions and handle time but no volume, and an Internal scenario would rest on the little history that Dynamics 365 holds.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Auto refresh isn't available when a forecast scenario uses an external data source, so the scenario can't be set up this way.
optionExplanations.e: Fails. An Internal scenario forecasts from history in Dynamics 365, and the 18 months of history sit in the retired application.

questions.prompt:
Pellworth Motor Club is moving its contact center to Dynamics 365 Contact Center and is reviewing its telephony provider. Breakdown calls are blind transferred to a non-Microsoft dispatch platform, and that workflow depends on SIP context such as caller ID, intent and authentication tokens. The voice design must stay in service after September 30, 2028.

You need to choose the telephony approach.

Which approach should you choose?

options.text: Teams Calling Plan numbers, with Microsoft as the carrier
Azure Communication Services Direct Routing through a customer-managed SBC
Teams Direct Routing through a customer-managed SBC
Azure Communication Services Direct Offer numbers, with Microsoft as the carrier

questions.answer: Teams Direct Routing through a customer-managed SBC.
questions.explanation: Two requirements decide this. Bring-your-own telephony is the documented fit for workflows that depend on SIP context, such as blind transfers and handoffs to non-Microsoft systems, while PSTN carriers outside the Microsoft network might strip that context from Microsoft calling plan numbers. Voice through Azure Communication Services, by Direct Routing or Direct Offer, is supported only through September 30, 2028. Teams Direct Routing meets both. Pellworth still owns the risk after a transfer: once a call goes back to its SBC, SIP context and call quality are its responsibility.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. SIP context might be stripped by PSTN carriers outside the Microsoft network, and this approach is best for use cases that don't need full SIP metadata.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. It preserves SIP context, but voice through Azure Communication Services is supported only through September 30, 2028.
optionExplanations.c: Correct. Teams Direct Routing is bring-your-own telephony, which preserves SIP context, and it isn't affected by the retirement.
optionExplanations.d: Fails on both requirements. SIP context might be stripped, and Direct Offer voice through Azure Communication Services is supported only through September 30, 2028.

questions.prompt:
Yarrow Family Health is keeping its non-Microsoft IVR. The IVR's SBC is connected through Azure direct routing to the Azure Communication Services resource that is connected to Dynamics 365 Contact Center, and the IVR's number is registered. The IVR transfers each call with a SIP INVITE, and its User-to-User header carries plain text key/value pairs for memberTier and visitReason.

Calls reach representatives, but routing rules and representatives cannot use either value. Nothing else has been added to the voice workstream, and Yarrow wants no custom development.

You need to make both values available for routing and to representatives.

What should you do?

options.text: Hex-encode the memberTier and visitReason payload at the IVR, and append ;encoding=hex to the User-to-User value.
In the workstream advanced settings, add one context variable named User-to-User to hold memberTier and visitReason.
In the workstream advanced settings, add context variables named memberTier and visitReason.
Turn on transcription in the workstream behaviors so that representatives can read the IVR conversation.

questions.answer: In the workstream advanced settings, add context variables named memberTier and visitReason.
questions.explanation: Getting the call across and getting the context across are separate checks. The SIP UUI payload is converted automatically into context data, but only for context variables on the voice workstream whose names match the parameter names in the header exactly. Yarrow already sends a supported format, so the missing piece is the variables, and no custom code is needed.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. Plain text key/value pairs are already a supported format. Changing the encoding does not create the context variables that receive the values.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. Context variable names must match the parameter names in the header, so memberTier and visitReason each need their own variable.
optionExplanations.c: Correct. Variables with these exact names let the payload convert into context data for routing and for representatives.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Call records and transcriptions from the non-Microsoft IVR call are not available to representatives, and a transcript would not supply routing values.

questions.prompt:
Lockhart Private Bank gives each wealth adviser a personal number with an inbound profile, so that clients can dial an adviser directly. Conversation orchestration is licensed and set up in the environment, and its playbook templates are available.

The bank has these requirements:
- If an adviser isn't available, including when the adviser is on another call, the client's call goes to the Adviser Support queue.
- If an adviser rejects the call, the client reaches voicemail.
- Other representatives' direct numbers keep their current behavior.

You need to meet the requirements.

What should you do?

options.text: Publish a playbook from the Manage overflow of incoming conversations using advanced conditions template, scoped to a list of queues, with an action for each condition.
Publish a playbook from the Handle overflow for direct inbound call template, scoped to the advisers' inbound profiles, with an action for each condition.
Enter the Adviser Support number in each adviser's Call forward field, and turn on Call transfer to external phone number in each inbound profile.
Use Handle rule-specific overflows in the voice workstream's route-to-queue rule, so that each adviser's direct calls overflow to the Adviser Support queue.

questions.answer: Publish a playbook from the Handle overflow for direct inbound call template, scoped to the advisers' inbound profiles, with an action for each condition.
questions.explanation: Direct inward dialing does not use unified routing, so queue overflow, queue playbooks and route-to-queue settings are the wrong tools. The direct inbound call playbook handles the direct call itself. The Handle overflow for direct inbound call template sets a separate action for when the user isn't available, rejects the notification, or lets it time out, and it can be scoped to a list of inbound profiles. That covers both requirements and leaves other direct numbers alone.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. That template acts on queues, with conditions such as no representatives available. It has no condition for one adviser rejecting a direct call, and direct inward dialing doesn't use unified routing.
optionExplanations.b: Correct. The template acts on the conditions in the requirements, the action list includes transferring to a queue and voicemail, and a list of inbound profiles limits the scope.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. Call forward sends a call to a PSTN number only when the status is DND or offline and the call is missed. A busy adviser's call goes to voicemail instead.
optionExplanations.d: Fails. Rule-specific overflow applies to a workstream's route-to-queue rules, and direct calls to a personal number do not go through unified routing.

questions.prompt:
Marlowe Language Schools supports students in many languages. Real-time translation is turned on and its web resource URL is set. Chat conversations are translated as expected.

Marlowe now wants representatives to see translated transcripts for voice calls too. Tenant, environment and consent prerequisites for voice features are met.

You need to add what translated voice transcripts require beyond the chat setup.

What should you do?

options.text: On the voice workstream's Language tab, add each student language, and configure its own voice settings.
In the real-time translation web resource file, set enableLanguageDetectionWithHistoryMessages to true.
On the Voice call experiences page, set Transcription & recording to Follow workstream settings for each external contact.
On the voice workstream's Behaviors tab, select Transcription and recording with Automatic start.

questions.answer: On the voice workstream's Behaviors tab, select Transcription and recording with Automatic start.
questions.explanation: Translated voice transcripts depend on more than the translation feature. Microsoft says you must enable call recording, transcription and real-time translation, so a voice workstream that captures nothing has nothing to translate. Chat translation working shows that the translation setup is sound, which points to capture on the voice workstream.

optionExplanations.a: Fails. Adding a language lets the voice channel serve that language with its own settings. It does not create a transcript to translate.
optionExplanations.b: Fails. Score-based language detection keeps translation from stopping when messages switch language. It does not supply a voice transcript.
optionExplanations.c: Fails. That setting applies only during a consult with or bridged transfer to an external contact, and it inherits the workstream configuration. It doesn't start capture on a student call.
optionExplanations.d: Correct. Call recording and transcription are required for translated voice transcripts to be displayed, and the stem says the voice prerequisites are met.

evidence.section: How forecast dates affect the data requirement
evidence.claim: Forecasting starts predicting on the day after the Historical End Date. Days before a later Forecast Start Date are the gap, and the gap counts toward the history you need. Available history is counted in calendar days.

evidence.claim: For short-term forecasts, required history including the gap is gap plus duration, and baseline history with no gap is the duration.

evidence.section: When history is insufficient; Short-term examples

Otherwise the queue and channel are skipped. Both cases are flagged Insufficient Historical Data.
evidence.applicability: The grace period is 15 days. The rows use different numbers from the article examples. evidence.section: Set up contextual call transfer using Azure direct routing
evidence.claim: Populate the SIP UUI header with context data, in plain text key/value pairs or a supported hex format. Create context variables with the same names in the workstream advanced settings, and make sure they match exactly with the param names in the SIP UUI header. The payload is automatically converted into context data for routing and for showing information to the representative.
evidence.applicability: The stem states the topology and a supported format, so only the variables are missing. The stem also rules out custom development, so a flow is not offered as an alternative. The procedure is specific to Azure Communication Services direct routing, which the stem states.

evidence.section: Use natural language playbooks to configure overflow actions for direct inward dialed calls; Use natural language playbooks to configure overflow actions for work items in queue
evidence.claim: By default, an unanswered direct call usually goes to voicemail. Conversation orchestration playbooks can run custom overflow actions. The Handle overflow for direct inbound call template is scoped to all inbound profiles, a list of inbound profiles, or all except some. Conditions are User rejects notification, User isn't available and User notification times out. Actions include Transfer to another queue and Send to voicemail. Save and publish the playbook. In the example, a representative on another call counts as not available. A separate queue playbook applies to all queues, selected queues or all queues except some, with queue conditions such as No representatives are available immediately and All representatives are signed out.
evidence.applicability: Supports the correct option. The stem puts a call in progress under unavailable, matching the page example. The queue playbook section explains why the option a decoy fails.

evidence.claim: Overflow handling has two templates. Manage overflow of incoming conversations using advanced conditions covers queue conditions, such as the queue being outside operating hours or no representatives being available, and is applied to all queues, a list of queues or all queues except some. Handle overflow for direct inbound call covers the target representative being unavailable, rejecting the call or not responding. A playbook is saved as a draft and activated with Publish.
evidence.applicability: The correct option says publish because a draft is not active. The stem says the feature is licensed and set up, which covers the prerequisites. Option a is the compliant decoy: a real template whose conditions act on queues. Opened 2026-11-07.

evidence.claim: Inbound profiles enable direct inward dialing and differ from workstreams, which route inbound calls through queues. Direct inward dialing does not use unified routing.
evidence.applicability: Explains why both the queue playbook and rule-specific overflow fail.

evidence.section: Enable call forwarding for personal phone numbers
evidence.claim: A call is forwarded to the PSTN number if the status is DND or offline and the representative misses the call. It is sent to voicemail if presence is Available, Away or Busy and the representative rejects or misses the call. The Call forward field takes a PSTN number.
evidence.applicability: Explains the Call forward distractor, which fails for an adviser on another call.

evidence.applicability: Status check for check 6. The manage-overflow page, dated Oct 30, 2026, has no preview label, but I could not confirm general availability. The stem states only that the playbook templates are available, and the answer does not depend on status.

evidence.section: Enable real-time translation of calls; Prerequisites; Enable call recording and transcription for voice
evidence.claim: To view translated voice transcripts for calls, you must enable call recording, transcription, and real-time translation. Recording needs the tenant-level audio recording toggle, the audio and mpeg MIME types, and Event Grid system topics. The Behaviors tab offers Transcription or Transcription and recording, with a Start setting.
evidence.applicability: The stem covers these prerequisites in one sentence. Microsoft does not say plainly whether Transcription alone is enough, and no option offers it, so the question does not depend on that gap.

evidence.section: Prerequisites; Enable real-time translation for representative and customer conversations; Enable score-based language detection
evidence.claim: Enable call recording and transcription for the translated voice call transcripts to be displayed. Score-based language detection is set with enableLanguageDetectionWithHistoryMessages and keeps translation from stopping when language switches.
evidence.applicability: Explains the correct option and the language detection distractor.

evidence.section: Add a phone number to the workstream and configure language settings
evidence.claim: You can add more languages to a voice channel, and each language has its own settings, so one number can serve several languages.
evidence.applicability: Explains the Language tab distractor.

evidence.section: Set up secure consult with and transfer to external contacts (preview)
evidence.claim: Transcription & recording is set under Consult and Bridged transfer for each external contact, and it indicates how recording and transcription are handled when the representative is consulting with or transferring a call to that contact. Follow workstream settings inherits the workstream configuration for transcription and recording.
evidence.applicability: Explains the option c decoy, which uses the same capture vocabulary as the correct option. The page labels this section a production-ready preview, and the decoy fails whatever its status. Page dated 2026-07-28, opened 2026-11-07.
